question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with a joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=3({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}),\,0\le y\le x\le 1.
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{Y}(y).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le x\le 1\}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272472/assets/2cc3b27a1f926e9f5b5fdf59a5ea01fb7e28da53c7fc01535cc590f4c315258c.png)

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{y}^{1}3({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{y}^{1}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}]}_{x=y}^{x=1} \\  & ={[{x}^{3}+3x{y}^{2}]}_{x=y}^{x=1} \\  & =[({1}^{3}+3\cdot 1\cdot {y}^{2})-({y}^{3}+3\cdot y\cdot {y}^{2})] \\  & =1+3{y}^{2}-4{y}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}1+3{y}^{2}-4{y}^{3}, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
